mo_future_cave_the.blurb: A large overhanging cave in the sandstone bouldering zone of Peter's Branch, in the Mark Twain National Forest of southwest Missouri. It holds around 21 boulder problems and is where the hardest lines in the whole zone live. The grades start around V2 but the weight sits well above that, with plenty of problems from V8 through V13 and only a handful in the easy-to-moderate range. The style is steep and sustained, closer to sport climbing for boulderers than to short highball blocs. Reaching it means following the trail from a neighbouring cliff, southwest and over the creek; the cave is hard to miss. Best for strong climbers.

mo_roadside.blurb: A compact band of sandstone beside the highway leading toward the main Peter's Branch bouldering zone, in southwest Missouri's Mark Twain National Forest. About 20 boulder problems are packed into a small stretch of quality stone. Difficulty runs from V3 up to V10, with most of the weight in the upper-middle range, so it suits climbers already comfortable on V6 to V9 more than beginners. Because the rock sits so close to the pavement, the landing zone includes a ditch and spotters often end up standing on the road shoulder; plan pads and spotting carefully.

mo_b_upper_picnic_area.blurb: A cluster of granite boulders in the eastern part of Elephant Rocks State Park, close to the park kiosk. Roughly 20 boulder problems, nearly all easy: most fall between V0 and V2, with only a few reaching V3 or V4. Expect cracks, slabs, an arete and a small cave crack rather than steep power moves. The big-grained granite is rough on skin but grips very well. It is a good place for beginners and for warming up before harder blocs elsewhere in the park, though the park draws plenty of visitors, so weekdays are quieter.

mt_prospector_crag.blurb: A newly developed crag in the Memorial Falls canyon above Belt Creek, near Neihart. Cliffs here stand roughly 80 to 150 feet, built from a pinkish, crystalline quartz that climbs a bit like a giant crystal. The mix is mostly trad, with sport lines and many top-rope setups, plus a couple of boulder problems. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.11, with the largest group at 5.10. Because the cliff is still being cleaned up, loose rock is possible; a helmet and careful belay positions are wise. Quiet and secluded, with a fun range for mixed-ability parties.

mt_practice_rock_2.blurb: A small crag in lower Hyalite Canyon, a short drive south of Bozeman, and one of the quickest places to squeeze in a climb after work. About 26 routes, mostly traditional with a few bolted lines and a single aid route. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, centred on 5.8 through 5.10, so it works for newer leaders as well as stronger climbers, and several routes can be top-roped. The cliff has south, west and north faces, giving sun and shade options through the day, though the west face can get hot. The walk from the roadside pullout is short.

mt_lower_nunnery.blurb: A roadside bouldering area in Gallatin Canyon, about half an hour south of Bozeman toward Big Sky, forming the lower part of the Nunnery boulder zone. Around 26 problems from V0 to V8, with most falling between V2 and V5 and just one real stretch above that, so it suits intermediate boulderers well. The blocks are spread over a main cluster plus a talus field, reached on a faint climber's trail from the highway turnout. Several boulders are big with awkward landings, so bring plenty of pads and a few spotters.
mt_lower_nunnery.parking_note: Use the large turnout on the east side of the Gallatin road, just past the pullout for the Cube sport crag. The first boulder is visible from there.

mt_black_line_buttress.blurb: A sizeable buttress on Gallatin Canyon's eastern wall, in the gneiss cliffs above the river on the way from Bozeman to Big Sky. It holds roughly 26 routes, nearly all traditional with a couple of bolted lines, and mixed-style possibilities. Grades begin around 5.8 and reach into the 5.13 range; the 5.10s are the biggest group, with 5.9, 5.11 and 5.12 each well represented. Expect a real hike up through the forest, with switchbacks on the steeper upper stretch. A good objective for confident trad leaders.
